newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes rise late on short covering, products - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes rise late on short covering, products - Sept 24.

text.p: U.S. crudes rose late Tuesday helped by short covering ahead of October pipeline scheduling and strength in gasoline futures, traders said.
A 70-cent spurt in NYMEX crude also filtered into the cash market but activity was confined mainly to small parcels.
"A few end-users pushed grades higher covering shorts," a Gulf Coast trader said, noting also better demand for some grades as a result of a tight import arbitrage.
Firm North Sea crude prices coupled with buoyant refinery runs, up 0.5 percent at 95.5 percent, according to the American Petroluem Institute (API) report, underpinned grades.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was valued around $24.50-60 a barrel, up about 70 cents from Monday.
The Oct/Nov WTI roll traded between 32 and 40 cents over the session, prompting WTI/Cushing Posting Plus to trade from $2.02 to $2.12 a barrel.
Refiners focused on completing Oct pipeline requirements with light, sweet grades gaining some upward momentum.
Oct Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded between WTI minus 22-15 cents, barely changed from Monday.
WTI/Midland chalked up the widest gains, moving up to WTI plus nine-12 cents, up from parity-eight cents previously.

The API report showing a draw of 2.1 million barrels in Gulf Coast crude stocks, a drop of 1.5 million barrels in the Midwest, and a draw of 831,000 barrels in stocks nationwide, added moderate support.
But traders said overall emphasis remained on a products shortfall, with heating oil and gasoline seen endangered by potential run cuts due to poor refining margins.
